justice: Wide, flat pedestrian sidewalks provide excellent physical accessibility for wheelchair users and the elderly
The absence of visible tactile paving on the pathways reduces fairness for visually impaired users
Dedicated, separated lanes for cars, bicycles, and pedestrians demonstrate an equitable distribution of road space among all road users
safety: White fences with planter boxes effectively separate motor vehicles from cyclists, significantly enhancing safety for adolescent and adult riders
Wide green verges act as a physical buffer between pedestrian sidewalks and active traffic, protecting socially vulnerable groups
Prominent streetlights equipped with surveillance cameras provide social surveillance (eyes on the street), increasing perceived security for all users
livability: The complete lack of street benches or resting facilities negatively impacts livability, especially for elderly individuals requiring periodic rests
The absence of active ground-floor retail or visible community activity creates a sterile, low-vitality environment
While nearby high-density residential towers suggest a large population, the street-level design lacks elements that encourage social interaction or lingering
sustainability: Dedicated, wide non-motorized vehicle lanes strongly encourage low-carbon, sustainable active travel like cycling
Continuous grass verges and planted tree strips provide permeable surfaces for natural rainwater infiltration
The street trees are relatively young with small canopies, currently limiting their ecological contribution to microclimate regulation and carbon absorption
aesthetics: Uniform white fencing, matching planter boxes, and modern streetlights create a highly cohesive and visually orderly streetscape
The asphalt road surface is impeccably clean and well-maintained, with crisp white lane markings enhancing visual appeal
The architectural contrast between the modern commercial facades on the left and the residential towers on the right adds structured visual variety
comfort: Young street trees offer minimal canopy cover, leading to poor thermal comfort (lack of shade) for pedestrians and the elderly during hot weather
The lack of public seating options diminishes physical comfort for socially vulnerable groups who cannot walk continuously for long distances
The spacious layout and clear segregation of traffic modes prevent crowding, providing high psychological comfort by reducing sensory overload
walkability: The paved sidewalks are sufficiently wide and flat, supporting safe and unimpeded walking for the elderly and mobility-impaired
A continuous green planted buffer between the sidewalk and the road shields pedestrians from traffic proximity, enhancing the walking experience
The long, straight block design without visible mid-block crosswalks may force pedestrians to take longer detours, reducing walking convenience
bikeability: Spacious, dedicated non-motorized side lanes provide an excellent, unimpeded right-of-way specifically for cyclists and scooters
Continuous physical barriers (fences and flower boxes) eliminate sideswipe conflicts with motor vehicles, ensuring a low-stress environment for cyclists of all ages
The smooth, newly paved asphalt surface in the bike lanes ensures a physically comfortable and highly efficient ride
